probe_policy.note: Open probes are adaptive: they fire where the Likert pattern carries signal (an extreme score or an internal spread), not on every competency. This keeps the session completable while still collecting qualitative depth where it matters. `not_observed` is the exception to 'where the ratings carry signal' — it fires on the absence of a rating, because a rater who cannot assess a competency is the one person whose partial view would otherwise be lost entirely. It is always optional to answer.

C1.low: You rated {subject}'s {competency} on the lower side. Without naming anyone else, what does a missed commitment usually look like in practice here?
C1.high: You rated {subject}'s {competency} highly. Can you describe a specific delivery where that reliability made a visible difference?
C1.mixed: Your ratings on {subject}'s {competency} were uneven. Which part holds up well, and which part tends to slip?
C1.not_observed: You marked part of {competency} as not observed, which is useful in itself. Is there anything you have seen about how {subject} handles commitments — even indirectly? "Nothing to add" is a perfectly good answer.
C1.default: Thinking about {subject}'s {competency}, what is one concrete example that shaped your rating?

C2.low: Where does {subject} most often need a nudge before things move forward?
C2.high: Can you describe a situation where {subject} took something end-to-end with no supervision at all?
C2.mixed: {subject} seems strong on some parts of autonomy and less so on others. Where does the line fall?
C2.not_observed: You have not seen enough of {competency} to rate it. Is there anything about how independently {subject} works that you have picked up, even second-hand? Feel free to say nothing to add.
C2.default: What does {subject}'s level of autonomy look like on a typical piece of work?

C3.low: What kinds of decisions does {subject} tend to escalate that you would expect them to make themselves?
C3.high: Can you describe a decision {subject} made under uncertainty that turned out well?
C3.mixed: How would you describe the gap between the quality of {subject}'s decisions and their willingness to make them?
C3.not_observed: {competency} was outside what you have observed. Is there anything about how {subject} approaches decisions you would still want on record? "Nothing to add" is fine.
C3.default: How does {subject} behave when a call has to be made without complete information?

C4.low: What is one process {subject} owns that has stayed manual or dependent on them being present?
C4.high: What has {subject} simplified or automated that the team still benefits from?
C4.mixed: {subject} appears to improve some things but not others. What explains the difference?
C4.not_observed: You marked {competency} as not observed. Have you noticed anything about how {subject} approaches improving the way work gets done? Say nothing to add if not.
C4.default: What has {subject} changed about how the work gets done since you started working with them?

C5.low: Where do {subject}'s priorities most often diverge from what the business needs?
C5.high: Can you describe an occasion where {subject} moved something forward that was bigger than their own remit?
C5.mixed: {subject}'s impact seems uneven across the business. Where does it land, and where does it stop?
C5.not_observed: {competency} is outside your line of sight. Is there anything about {subject}'s effect beyond their own tasks that you have noticed anyway? "Nothing to add" is fine.
C5.default: Beyond their own tasks, where do you see the effect of {subject}'s work?

C6.low: What does {subject} tend to miss about the customer's actual problem?
C6.high: Can you describe a time {subject} went past the stated request to solve the real problem?
C6.mixed: How does {subject}'s customer focus change between internal and external customers?
C6.not_observed: You have not seen enough of {competency} to judge it. Is there anything about how {subject} treats the people their work serves that you would still add? Nothing to add is a fine answer.
C6.default: Does {subject} work to finish a task, or to solve the underlying problem? What makes you say that?

B1.not_observed: You marked {competency} as not observed. Is there anything about working alongside {subject} that you would still want to mention? "Nothing to add" is fine.
B1.default: How does {subject} behave when work has to be shared across several people who disagree about the approach?

B2.not_observed: {competency} was outside what you have seen. Have you noticed anything about the effect {subject} has on other people's growth? Say nothing to add if not.
B2.default: What has someone else learned to do because of {subject}?

B3.not_observed: You have not seen enough of {competency} to rate it. Is there anything about {subject}'s willingness to help that you have picked up anyway? "Nothing to add" is fine.
B3.default: When someone needs help outside {subject}'s objectives, what actually happens?

B4.low: What kind of problem keeps coming back after {subject} has handled it?
B4.high: What did the team learn to handle on its own after {subject} solved something?
B4.not_observed: {competency} is outside what you have observed. Is there anything about how {subject} deals with problems that you would still add? Nothing to add is a perfectly good answer.
B4.default: After {subject} resolves an issue, is the team more able to handle a similar one? What makes you say that?

followup_templates.needs_example: That is useful. Can you ground it in one specific occasion — roughly when it happened and what you observed?
followup_templates.needs_behaviour: Could you describe what {subject} actually did or said, rather than the overall impression it left?
followup_templates.needs_effect: And what changed as a result — for the work, the team, or the customer?
followup_templates.too_short: Could you say a little more? Even two or three sentences of detail helps the person receiving this.

qualitative_fixed.prompt: Describe a recent situation where {subject}'s delivery or decision-making prevented a problem or produced a strong result.
In which areas does {subject} already act as a senior or reference point for the team?
What should {subject} start doing, or stop doing, to increase their impact and autonomy?
What skills or attitudes is {subject} missing for their next career step?
